tools.name: select_volume
tools.description: Switch a pane to a volume from cmdr://state, preferably by volumeId (names can collide). The pane reopens the folder last used there; the tool replies once it rests. To move within the current volume, use nav_to_path.

name.description: Legacy selector: a unique volume name from cmdr://state. Prefer volumeId.

volumeId.description: Stable volume id from cmdr://state. Preferred because names can collide; wins when both selectors are supplied.

tools.name: nav_to_path
tools.description: Navigate a pane to a path: absolute, ~-relative, or mtp:// (smb:// is not navigable; reach a share with select_volume). Prefer this over nav_to_parent when you know the target. Archive paths are transparent, so foo.zip/inner navigates inside the archive.

path.description: Path to navigate to: absolute, ~-relative, or mtp://. An smb:// path is refused: a mounted share is its own volume (select_volume by the name in cmdr://state volumes), and an unmounted one opens from the Network volume's host list.

tools.name: nav_to_parent
tools.description: Navigate the focused pane up to its parent folder.

tools.name: nav_back
tools.description: Go back to the focused pane's previous folder in its navigation history.

tools.name: nav_forward
tools.description: Go forward again (undo a nav_back) in the focused pane's navigation history.

tools.name: scroll_to
tools.description: Load the file window around an index in a large (paginated) directory so those rows appear in cmdr://state. Needed before move_cursor / select can reach a row outside the currently loaded range.

tools.name: move_cursor
tools.description: Focus a pane and move its cursor to a row, by zero-based index or by filename (give one). Flushes pane state, so a following copy / move / delete / rename acts on this row. A missing filename or out-of-range index is an honest error, never a silent no-op.

pane.description: Which pane to move cursor in

index.description: Zero-based index to move cursor to

tools.name: open_under_cursor
tools.description: Open the item under the cursor, like pressing Enter: enter a folder, open a file, or connect a network host / share. A person confirms a file or app first; a folder just opens.

tools.name: select
tools.description: Select files in a pane by names, by an index range (start + count), or all; count=0 clears. Focuses the pane and flushes state, so a following copy / move / delete / compress acts on this selection. names errors if any name isn't in the listing.

names.description: Filenames to select. Errors if any name isn't in the listing.

count.description: Number of items from start. 0 clears selection

tools.name: copy
tools.description: Open the dialog that copies a pane's selection into the folder the other pane shows; already there duplicates each as name (1). A person confirms it, so nothing has happened yet when this returns. Refuses with nothing selected. onConflict presets the dialog's choice for clashes.

pane.description: The pane to copy from; the other pane's folder is the destination.

onConflict.description: What the dialog's 'files already exist' choice opens on, for clashing FILES. A person still confirms, and can change it. Omit for their saved choice. Folders always merge. 'stop' asks per file. overwrite_smaller_all / overwrite_older_all overwrite only when the destination is strictly smaller / older, and skip otherwise.

tools.name: move
tools.description: Open the dialog that moves a pane's selection to the other pane. A person confirms it, so nothing has happened yet when this returns. Refuses with nothing selected. onConflict presets the dialog's choice for clashes.

pane.description: The pane to move from; the other pane's folder is the destination.

onConflict.description: What the dialog's 'files already exist' choice opens on, for clashing FILES. A person still confirms, and can change it. Omit for their saved choice. Folders always merge. 'stop' asks per file. overwrite_smaller_all / overwrite_older_all overwrite only when the destination is strictly smaller / older, and skip otherwise.

tools.name: compress
tools.description: Open the dialog that zips a pane's selection (else its cursor item) into a new archive in the other pane. A person confirms it, so nothing has happened yet when this returns.

pane.description: The pane to compress from; the archive lands in the other pane's folder.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Open the dialog that deletes a pane's selection (else its cursor item). A person confirms it, so nothing has happened yet when this returns. mode presets trash vs permanent; omit for the pane's default.

mode.description: What the dialog opens on: trash = move to Trash; delete = permanent. Omit for the pane's default (a volume without a trash forces permanent).

tools.name: rename
tools.description: Open the inline rename editor on an item (the named item, else the cursor item) in a pane, prefilled with newName. A person confirms it, so nothing has happened yet when this returns.

name.description: Current filename to rename. Defaults to the cursor item. Errors if it isn't in the listing.

newName.description: The proposed new name (a name, not a path).

tools.name: multi_rename
tools.description: Pattern-rename the pane's files with the Multi-Rename Tool's settings (masks, search and replace, case, counter; every one optional). dryRun (default) previews each row's new name and status, paged with start/limit. dryRun false stages every ready row as ONE rename proposal for the user to review and approve in Cmdr; it never renames anything itself.

pane.description: Which pane's files to rename. Defaults to the focused pane.

names.description: File names in the pane's folder, in rename order (what [C] counts by). Defaults to the selection, else the cursor item.

nameMask.description: Name mask (default [N]). Placeholders: [N] name, [N2-5] / [N-3] ranges, [E] extension, [C] counter ([C10+5:3] = start 10, step 5, 3 digits), [P] parent folder, [G] grandparent, [Y] [M] [D] [h] [m] [s] and [YMD] modified time, [U] / [L] / [F] / [n] upper, lower, words, or original case for what follows. [[ is a literal [. Media fields read each file's EXIF and tags: [=exif.taken:YMD] (date taken; [=exif.taken|modified:YMD] falls back to the modified date), exif.camera / make / model / lens / iso / focal / width / height / orientation, tag.title / artist / albumartist / album / track / disc / year / genre / comment ([=tag.track:2] pads to two digits). A file without the field is a noValue row, one that can't be read unreadable. A call reads at most 2,000 media files; past that it's refused as specError tooManyMediaFiles.

search.description: Search for this in the name (default nothing). a|b with replace x|y swaps in one pass.

firstOnly.description: Replace only the first match (default false).

regex.description: search is a regular expression (default false).

substitute.description: With regex: $1 in replace inserts a group (default false).

case.description: Case step after search and replace (default unchanged).

removeDiacritics.description: Strip accents from Latin and Greek letters (default false).

greekToLatin.description: Write Greek letters in Latin ones, ELOT 743 (default false).

normalizeUnicode.description: Rename to the composed (NFC) Unicode form (default false).

dryRun.description: true (default): preview only. false: stage every ready row as ONE rename proposal the user reviews and approves in Cmdr. Nothing is ever renamed by this tool.

start.description: Dry run: first row of the page (default 0).

limit.description: Dry run: rows per page (default 50, max 200).

filter.description: Dry run: page every row (default) or only the ones that can't be renamed as set.

rationale.description: Proposal only: why, shown to the user as your words.

tools.name: mkdir
tools.description: Create a folder in a pane. A name creates it directly (errors on a name conflict); no name opens the naming dialog for a person.

name.description: Folder name: creates it directly. Omit to open the naming dialog for a person.

tools.name: mkfile
tools.description: Create an empty file in a pane. A name creates it directly (errors on a name conflict); no name opens the naming dialog for a person.

name.description: File name: creates it directly. Omit to open the naming dialog for a person.

tools.name: refresh
tools.description: Force a re-read of the focused pane's listing (from disk on local volumes; the watcher cache short-circuits on MTP / SMB). Use after an out-of-band change; navigation and file ops already refresh on their own.

tools.name: tag
tools.description: Set macOS Finder color tags on files by name (else selection, else cursor). set: make the colors exactly (keeps colorless tags). toggle: flip each color. clear: remove all. macOS only; tags show in cmdr://state as [tags:red,blue]. The answer names the operationId; operations_rollback puts back every file's prior tags.

names.description: Filenames to tag. Defaults to the pane's selection, and refuses with neither. Errors if a name isn't in the listing.

colors.description: Finder color names. Required for set and toggle; ignored for clear.

tools.name: toggle_hidden
tools.description: Toggle whether hidden (dotfile) files show in the file lists (the showHidden flag in cmdr://state).

tools.name: set_view_mode
tools.description: Set a pane's view mode: brief (names, only the cursor row detailed) or full (size and date on every row). full makes cmdr://state carry those details for all rows, not just the cursor.

pane.description: Which pane to set view mode for

tools.name: sort
tools.description: Sort a pane by a field (name, ext, size, modified, created) and order (asc / desc).

tools.name: tab
tools.description: Manage a pane's tabs: new, close, close_others, activate, set_pinned, reopen (restore the last-closed tab), or move (reorder with toIndex, or send to the other pane with toPane). tabId defaults to the active tab where it applies; see each pane's tabs in cmdr://state.

action.description: Action to perform on the tab

pane.description: Which pane to operate on. For move: the pane the tab is in now.

tabId.description: Tab ID. Defaults to active tab for close, close_others, set_pinned, move. Required for activate. Not used for new or reopen.

toPane.description: For move: the pane the tab goes to. Defaults to `pane` (a reorder). A move never activates the tab or changes pane focus, and is refused for a pinned tab, a pane's only tab, or a pane at its tab limit.

toIndex.description: For move: the 0-based index the tab holds once moved, as `i:` in cmdr://state then shows it. Defaults to the end; a larger index also means the end. move needs toPane, toIndex, or both.

tools.name: dialog
tools.description: Open, focus, or close a dialog. Open/focus: settings, file-viewer, about. Close: any id from cmdr://dialogs/available. cmdr://state lists what's open.

type.description: Dialog type. Openable/focusable: settings, file-viewer, about. Closable: any dialog id from cmdr://dialogs/available (also settings, file-viewer). 'close' on quit-confirmation calls the quit off and keeps what's running; the quit tool raises it, never 'open'. 'close' on rename ends the inline rename editor without saving.

section.description: For settings: which section to open, by its sidebar name (e.g., 'Keyboard shortcuts'). cmdr://settings groups every setting under these names.

path.description: For file-viewer: file path. On open without path, uses cursor file. On close without path, closes all.

tools.name: dialog_confirm
tools.description: Press Confirm on an open dialog, or commit the inline rename editor, in a person's place. cmdr://state lists what's open.

type.description: What to confirm: transfer-confirmation (covers copy and move; 'copy-confirmation' is an alias), delete-confirmation, rename (the inline editor), mkdir-confirmation, new-file-confirmation, rollback-confirmation (answers { status, inverseOpId }, or { status: 'refused', refusal }), or quit-confirmation (quits now and stops what's running). A confirm on transfer-confirmation or delete-confirmation returns the started operation's id ('operationId: <id>' in the OK text) for await operation_complete or queue. A delete-confirmation trash of a cloud-drive folder answers once the folder's scan rules out online-only files, which can take up to about 90 seconds. A press the dialog itself stopped (a refused source, a press already in flight) refuses with data.refusal = 'notStarted' and leaves the dialog open.

name.description: For rename, mkdir-confirmation, and new-file-confirmation: the name to commit. Omit to commit what the field holds. A name that doesn't stick refuses with data.refusal = 'nameRefused' and leaves it open. A rename that copies too much to start unasked refuses with data.refusal = 'needsMoveDialog', having opened the Move dialog.

background.description: For transfer-confirmation or delete-confirmation: press the dialog's Background button (F2) instead of Confirm, so the operation starts with no progress dialog. A delete only runs in the background as a trash: a dialog set to delete permanently refuses with data.refusal = 'permanentDelete' and stays open. Default: false

onConflict.description: For transfer-confirmation: conflict resolution policy for clashing FILES. Folders always merge (a source folder landing on a same-named dest folder merges into it), and this policy governs the files inside. 'stop' decides nothing upfront: the operation asks per file and parks until you answer each one with resolve_conflict (watch cmdr://state operations for the pendingConflict block). The *_all policies decide every clash upfront. overwrite_smaller_all / overwrite_older_all overwrite only when the destination is strictly smaller / strictly older, and skip otherwise. Default: the policy the dialog shows.

tools.name: open_search_dialog
tools.description: Open the search dialog with optional pre-filled query and filters. If autoRun (default true), runs the search immediately. Acks once the dialog has mounted; does not wait for results to render.

query.description: Search query to pre-fill in the search bar

mode.description: Search mode. Defaults to 'ai' if AI is enabled, otherwise 'filename'.

isDirectory.description: Type filter: true = folders only, false = files only, omit for both

scope.description: Scope string, same syntax as the scope chip: comma-separated paths, ! prefix for excludes

excludeSystemDirs.description: Exclude system/build/cache folders (node_modules, .git, Caches, etc.). Defaults on; turn it off for disk-space questions, where those folders are usually the answer.

autoRun.description: Default true: open and run the search. False: open and prefill without running.

tools.name: quit
tools.description: Quit Cmdr, via the gate Cmd-Q uses. Nothing running: outcome 'quitting'. A copy, move, or delete still going: it does NOT quit; 'held' names them and the ms left, and a person answers quit-confirmation or the countdown quits anyway. A person confirms first.

tools.name: switch_pane
tools.description: Toggle focus to the other pane. Takes no parameters. To focus a SPECIFIC pane, use select (with count 0 to clear) or select_volume / nav_to_path on that pane, which focus it.

tools.name: swap_panes
tools.description: Swap left and right pane directories, view modes, sort orders, and selections

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find files and folders across ONE whole drive by name pattern, size, date, or type. list_dir ranks one folder's children instead. Reads the index and walks the rest, so an unindexed drive still answers, only slower. Names and metadata only: inspect_file reads contents, and a date is when a file last CHANGED, never saved or opened. Disk space: sortBy size with excludeSystemDirs false. No paging, so narrow instead. Cover the drive the question is about and say which one you covered.

pattern.description: Glob or regex filename pattern (for example, "*.pdf", "report*")

sizeMin.description: Minimum file size, human-readable (for example, "1 MB", "500 KiB")

modifiedAfter.description: ISO date, for example "2025-01-01": files modified on or after the start of that day in the user's local time zone

modifiedBefore.description: ISO date: files modified before the start of that day in the user's local time zone

type.description: Filter by type. Omit for both.

scope.description: Scope string: comma-separated paths, ! for excludes (for example, "~/projects, !node_modules"). A search covers ONE volume, so every include path must be on the same drive; omit to search the boot volume.

volumeId.description: From list_volumes: search its whole root, or the scope's paths on it. Works when not connected, from its index.

caseSensitive.description: Case-sensitive matching. Default: false on macOS, true on Linux

excludeSystemDirs.description: Skip system, cache, and build folders (node_modules, .git, Caches). Default: true.

sortBy.description: relevance (default), size (biggest first, a folder by its recursive total), or modified (newest first).

countOnly.description: Answer with the counts and coverage alone, no entries. Default: false.

limit.description: Max entries. Default 30, max 200; a page may come back shorter to fit one result.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for the walk, 1-120. Default: 20.

tools.name: ai_search
tools.description: Search with a natural-language query; the configured LLM turns it into a structured search over one drive, reading the index and walking whatever it hasn't covered. Use search instead when you can express the query as a pattern or filter (no LLM call).

query.description: Natural language search query (for example, "recent invoices marked rymd")

scope.description: Scope string: comma-separated paths, ! for excludes (for example, "~/projects, !node_modules"). Merged with AI-inferred scope. A search covers ONE volume, so every include path must be on the same drive; omit to search the boot volume.

limit.description: Max results to return. Default 30, max 200.

maxWaitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the search, 1-120 (on top of the LLM translation, which runs first). Cmdr walks whatever the index hasn't covered yet, so a first search of a folder takes as long as reading it does. When the wait runs out you get what was found so far plus a note. Default: 20

tools.name: set_setting
tools.description: Set a setting value. Use the cmdr://settings resource to discover available settings and their constraints. A setting marked mcpSettable: false there is refused; one marked mcpSettable: offOnly accepts only false. A person confirms the change first, seeing the old and new value, unless the setting is marked safe.

tools.name: indexing
tools.description: Control one volume's drive indexing. Actions: enable (on, starts first scan), disable (off, keeps DB), rescan (fresh full scan), forget (delete DB). enable/rescan return once scanning starts; poll await index_status fresh for done. See cmdr://indexing. A person confirms first.

volumeId.description: Volume ID to control (for example 'root', 'smb-…', 'mtp-…:1'). See cmdr://state volumes.

tools.name: queue
tools.description: Control the operation queue: pause / resume / cancel one operationId, or pause_all / resume_all. cancel keeps what's written, and also takes operationIds (array) for several; operations_rollback asks a person to undo it instead. continue_without_gone answers a pendingSourcesGone question; skip_locked answers a pendingLockedSources one. See cmdr://state operations for ids.

action.description: pause | resume | cancel | continue_without_gone | skip_locked | pause_all | resume_all. pause acts on a running operation; a queued one isn't touching a device yet, so pausing it is refused rather than silently ignored. cancel keeps what's already written. continue_without_gone answers an operation's pendingSourcesGone question by carrying on with the sources still there (cancel is the other answer). skip_locked answers a move's pendingLockedSources question by leaving the Locked items where they are and moving the rest (cancel is another answer).

operationId.description: Operation to act on (required for pause / resume / cancel / continue_without_gone / skip_locked unless operationIds is given). See cmdr://state operations.

operationIds.description: For cancel only: several operations to cancel at once.

tools.name: queue_move_locked
tools.description: Answer a move's pendingLockedSources question in a person's place: unlock its Locked items for the move, and lock each again where it lands. See cmdr://state operations for ids.

operationId.description: The move parked on a pendingLockedSources question. See cmdr://state operations.

tools.name: resolve_conflict
tools.description: Answer ONE name clash a running operation is parked on: skip / overwrite / rename that file, applyToAll for the rest. Read cmdr://state operations first for the pendingConflict block. Returns a typed outcome; refuses rather than pretending.

operationId.description: The operation parked on the clash. From the pendingConflict block in cmdr://state operations.

conflictId.description: Which clash of that operation you're answering, from the same pendingConflict block. Required: an operation raises its clashes one at a time, and naming the one you saw is what stops your answer from landing on the next one.

resolution.description: skip leaves the destination alone | overwrite replaces it | rename keeps both (the copy lands as 'name (1).ext') | overwrite_smaller and overwrite_older replace only when the destination is strictly smaller / strictly older, and skip otherwise.

applyToAll.description: Apply this answer to every later clash in the same operation, so it stops asking. Default false: this answers one file.

tools.name: unlock
tools.description: Answer the password prompt for a locked archive or backup repo in cmdr://state, naming its path. A repo checks the password first: wrong_password means nothing was kept. browse mode: it re-lists and you're in. transfer mode: it hands over the password ONLY, since supplying one never starts a write; run copy or move again to extract.

path.description: Which locked archive or backup repo you're answering, copied verbatim from the path on the archive-password entry in cmdr://state dialogs. Required: another surface may have answered the prompt you read and a different one may be asking now.

password.description: The password to try. Handed to the archive or repo only, never echoed back, never rendered in cmdr://state, never logged, and never saved to the Keychain.

tools.name: favorites
tools.description: Manage the user's favorites (the bookmarked folders the favorites menu lists). add: path (+ optional name). rename: id + name. remove: id. reorder: orderedIds, the COMPLETE new ordering. Discover ids in cmdr://state favorites.

path.description: For add: the folder to favorite, on a disk, a share, a server (sftp://, webdav://, s3://), or a phone (mtp://, adb://) that is connected now (~ expands to home).

id.description: For rename / remove: the favorite id. See cmdr://state favorites.

name.description: For add (optional, defaults to the path's name) / rename (required): the display label.

orderedIds.description: For reorder: the complete new ordering of favorite ids.

tools.name: connect_to_server
tools.description: Add a manual SMB server by address. Checks TCP reachability then adds to the host list.

address.description: Server address: hostname, IP, IP:port, or smb:// URL

tools.name: remove_manual_server
tools.description: Remove a manually-added server from the host list. A person confirms first.

hostId.description: Host ID to remove (for example, manual-192-168-1-100-9445)

tools.name: upgrade_smb_to_direct
tools.description: Upgrade an OS-mounted SMB volume to a direct smb2 session for faster I/O. Uses Keychain creds. Returns OK or NeedsCredentials; a server it can't reach, a volume that's gone, or one that isn't an SMB mount comes back as an error. See cmdr://state volumes for each SMB share's connectionState.

volumeId.description: Volume ID of the SMB share (e.g. smb-192-168-1-111-445-naspi). See cmdr://state volumes.

tools.name: eject
tools.description: Detach a volume by id: eject a disk or disk image, unmount an SMB share, disconnect a phone, or close a connection to an SFTP or WebDAV server. The server stays saved. A volume of a disk that keeps others mounted goes alone, so that disk stays attached unless scope is disk. Answers which teardown ran; refuses (typed outcome in the error data) while an operation is using the volume, and for a volume that can't be detached at all. See cmdr://state volumes for ids. A person confirms first.

volumeId.description: Volume ID to detach (for example 'vol-…', 'smb-…', 'mtp-…:1', or 'sftp-…'). See cmdr://state volumes.

scope.description: How much of a physical disk to take down. 'volume' (the default) takes this volume alone while its disk keeps others mounted, and the disk with the last one. 'disk' takes every volume on the disk and the disk, refusing first with outcome 'heldBeforeEject' when someone is holding one.

tools.name: await
tools.description: Wait until a condition is met, after fire-and-forget actions or async events. Pane conditions watch a pane; index_status watches a volume's indexing freshness; operation_complete / operations_idle watch the write-operation queue.

pane.description: Which pane to watch. Required for the pane conditions; ignored for index_status / operation_complete / operations_idle.

condition.description: Condition to wait for: has_item / not_has_item (file list contains / no longer contains item named value — use not_has_item after a delete), item_count_gte / item_count_lte (file list has >= / <= value items), path (pane path equals value), path_contains (pane path contains value), index_status (volumeId's indexing freshness equals value: fresh / scanning / stale), operation_complete (the operation whose id is value settled — completed / cancelled / failed, reported in the result), operations_idle (no operation is running or queued; takes no value)

volumeId.description: For index_status: the volume whose indexing freshness to watch (for example 'root', 'smb-…', 'mtp-…:1').

value.description: Value for the condition (item name, count, path, substring, an index_status status fresh / scanning / stale, or for operation_complete the operationId). Not used by operations_idle.

afterGeneration.description: Only consider state updates after this generation number. Prevents matching stale state from before an action. Get the current generation from cmdr://state or a previous await result. Pane conditions only.

tools.name: go_to_latest_download
tools.description: Navigate the focused pane to the most recently observed eligible file in ~/Downloads and select it. Errors if no eligible file exists or Cmdr lacks Full Disk Access.

tools.name: operations_list
tools.description: List past operations (copy, move, delete, trash, rename, create, compress), newest first; filter by time, item name, kind, initiator, status; paged. In-flight ops: cmdr://state operations and the queue tool.

since.description: Start time at or after this (Unix ms).

until.description: Start time at or before this (Unix ms).

name.description: Item name to match (case- and Unicode-folded), exact or prefix per nameMatch; not a substring search.

limit.description: Default 50, max 1000; a page may come back shorter, with returned, total, and truncated; use offset for the rest.

tools.name: operations_get
tools.description: One operation's header plus a page of its item rows (source/dest paths, per-item outcome). Poll it to watch a rollback settle (rollbackState leaves 'rollingBack').

operationId.description: The operation's id, as given by operations_list, a copy/move/delete response, cmdr://state operations, or the queue tool.

limit.description: Default 200, max 1000; a page may come back shorter, with returned, total, and truncated; use offset for the rest.

tools.name: operations_rollback
tools.description: Ask a person to reverse an operation, finished or running: opens the rollback dialog, or refuses with a typed reason and no dialog when it can't roll back. A reversal deletes the copies, moves back, or restores from trash; it rechecks each item, never overwrites, and skips a drifted or occupied item. Answers awaitingPerson, and nothing has happened yet: once the dialog leaves cmdr://state dialogs, read rollbackState with operations_get.

operationId.description: The operation to reverse, finished or running. Same id as operations_list, a dialog_confirm response, or cmdr://state operations.

tools.name: search_photos
tools.description: Find photos by content: a scene description, text inside the image (OCR), or a tag, from the on-device index (no uploads). Returns matching paths plus a short reason. Omit mode to combine description + OCR. Needs image indexing on.

query.description: What to look for: a scene description (semantic), words expected IN the image (ocr), or one object/scene label (tag).

volumeId.description: One volume id (see list_volumes); omit for every indexed local and SMB volume.

mode.description: semantic: by visual description. ocr: by text recognized in the image. tag: by a Vision label. Omit to combine semantic + ocr, best for most photo questions.

limit.description: Max hits (default 30, max 200); a page may come back shorter, with returned, total, and truncated.

tools.name: image_facts
tools.description: What the image index stored for given images: the recognized text (OCR) plus Vision tags, per path, to name or describe files you already know. Up to 200 paths; each answers indexed or notIndexed. Needs image indexing on.

paths.description: Absolute image paths, at most 200. A page may hold fewer than asked: check returned, total, and truncated, then ask for the rest.

volumeId.description: One volume id (see list_volumes); omit for every indexed local and SMB volume.

tools.name: memory_diagnostics
tools.description: What this Cmdr process is holding right now: the physical footprint, the Rust heap tagged by the global allocator holding it (mimalloc or system) and split into live data and allocator slack, the other malloc zones, SQLite's page-cache slab, and the kernel's VM map folded by tag with a per-tag region-size histogram. The only reading that spans every allocator. macOS only.

sizesPerTag.description: Region-size groups to report per tag (default 8, clamped to 24). 0 asks for tag totals only. A repeated exact region size fingerprints whatever asked for those bytes.

tools.name: cpu_diagnostics
tools.description: Where this Cmdr process's CPU went over a window, per named thread: each live thread's CPU delta (and threads folded by name), what threads that exited inside the window spent (the process delta minus the live threads'), wakeups from TASK_POWER_INFO, context switches and syscalls, and how the thread count moved. 'measure' (default) blocks for windowSeconds; for longer windows, 'mark' a baseline and read 'sinceMark' later. Percentages are of one core. macOS only.

action.description: measure (default): block for windowSeconds, then report. mark: store a baseline and return at once. sinceMark: report from the last mark to now, without blocking; the mark stays, so repeated reads are cumulative.

windowSeconds.description: measure only: the window length (default 10). Longer windows: mark, then sinceMark.

maxThreads.description: Individual threads to list, costliest first (default 20). threadsByName always lists every name.

tools.name: read_resource
tools.description: Read a cmdr:// view, the way to follow any cmdr:// another tool mentions. cmdr://state (?include=panes,volumes,dialogs,listings,recentErrors,operations,favorites, ?compact=true), cmdr://settings (******** is private), cmdr://logs (redacted; ?since=<iso>&filter=<text>&limit=<n>), cmdr://indexing (?volume=<id>), cmdr://importance (?path=, ?top=&volume=, ?threshold=), cmdr://dialogs/available. truncated: true comes with nextOffset: pass it as offset for the rest.

uri.description: cmdr://state, cmdr://settings, cmdr://logs, cmdr://indexing, cmdr://importance, or cmdr://dialogs/available, with its query if any

offset.description: Characters to skip: the nextOffset of the answer before.

tools.name: app_state
tools.description: Snapshot the live app state: both panes (folder, cursor item, selection, view mode, sort) and the mounted volumes with index freshness and connectivity: what the user is looking at right now.

tools.name: inspect_file
tools.description: Look inside files: metadata, the format the bytes really are, and per kind the content: a line window of text (any encoding), PDF text by page, an archive's entries (a zip, tar, or 7z, or a path inside one), or an image's dimensions and camera data (then image_facts for what's in it). find searches text files and PDFs. Up to 200 paths; every cut is reported.

paths.description: Absolute file paths (~ ok), at most 200; check returned, total, truncated, and unanswered.

find.description: Search text files and PDFs; matching lines replace the window.

tools.name: propose_rename_plan
tools.description: Stage a same-folder image-file rename plan for the user to review; it changes nothing and approves nothing. At most 200 rows.

evidence.description: What the name is based on; the user sees it, and a content claim is checked against what image_facts returned to you.

source.description: imageText or imageTags only when image_facts returned that content for this exact path in this conversation; else filename (the old name), metadata (dates, size), or userInstruction (a rule the user gave).

detail.description: Up to 160 characters. imageText: a VERBATIM quote of at least 12 characters (a phrase, not one word) from what image_facts returned for this path; imageTags: a tag it returned; else the concrete detail used, like 'Taken 2026-07-20'.

tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: List a folder's children and recursive size from the drive index. An unindexed folder is read live, without folder sizes; a volume that isn't connected answers from its last index, dated. sortBy size finds where space goes inside ONE folder; search ranks a whole drive.

path.description: Absolute or ~-relative folder to list. Relay the coverage block and any lower-bound size rather than a total the index can't back.

volumeId.description: From list_volumes or a result's location; omit for a path on a connected volume.

sortBy.description: size ranks files and folders together by space used (a folder by its recursive total). Default name.

order.description: Default desc for size and modified, asc for name.

limit.description: Default 50, max 1000; a page may come back shorter to fit one result.

offset.description: Children to skip; resume with offset + returned.

type.description: Only files or only folders; omit for both.

tools.name: list_pane_files
tools.description: List up to 200 entries of the focused pane from its listing cache, never the index or disk. A selection hides the folder's other rows: scope says which you got. Its location is the volume ID and parent path a rename proposal needs.

tools.name: important_folders
tools.description: List the most important folders across scored volumes, highest first, each a location with its score and why. A row's folded counts near-duplicate subfolders merged into it; pass its location as under + volumeId to list them. Works offline, so an unmounted-but-scored drive still answers.

top.description: Default 20; ignored when threshold is set.

threshold.description: Every folder scoring at or above this (0-1) instead of a top-N.

volumeId.description: From list_volumes or a row's location; omit for every scored volume.

under.description: Only folders at or below this one (on volumeId when given); ~ ok.

tools.name: folder_importance
tools.description: Explain one folder's importance: scored (0-1 score, signal breakdown, and whether it is stale since the latest scan), floored to zero by design (with the reason), or unscored. Works offline.

volumeId.description: From list_volumes or a result's location; omit for a path on a connected volume.

tools.name: list_suggestions
tools.description: List the operations Ask Cmdr already proposed, as sweeps and groups with op COUNTS, never the ops. Default status pending: what still waits on the user.

status.description: Default pending: still waiting on the user. interrupted: the app restarted mid-execution, so the user decides again.

tools.name: get_suggestion_group
tools.description: Read one proposed group: verb, target, reversibility, and a page of the files it would act on (total / returned / truncated; page with offset). Sizes and dates are what the index held when the group was proposed, not the files now.

offset.description: Ops to skip; resume with offset + returned.

limit.description: Default 100, max 500; a page may come back shorter when paths are long.

tools.name: propose_suggestions
tools.description: Propose file operations for the user to review. It stages a proposal and changes nothing: only the user approves. Name up to 200 paths per group, or describe thousands with a selector, resolved against the drive index once, now. A whole folder is ONE op: give its path. A place on a volume that isn't connected refuses. sweepId plus groupId replaces a pending group you proposed.

sweepId.description: Add to or amend this sweep. Required with any groupId.

rationale.description: Your reason for the sweep, shown as your words.

groups.description: Each group is approved or rejected on its own.

groupId.description: A pending group of this sweep to rewrite whole.

destination.description: Destination folder (move, copy, extract) or archive path (compress).

overwritesExisting.description: compress only: that archive exists, so the group can't be undone.

parent.description: rename only: the folder every source shares.

sourceVolumeId.description: The sources' volume. With paths or renames; a selector supplies its own.

displayName.description: The group's title. With paths or renames; a selector is named by its pattern.

rationale.description: Why this group, shown as your words.

paths.description: Sources by absolute path. A folder's path is ONE op.

renames.description: rename, move, copy: each source and its new bare name. Move or copy: list every file; its current name keeps it.

selector.description: Propose over a pattern instead of a list. Not for rename.

nameGlob.description: Glob over the file name, such as *.dmg.

olderThanDays.description: Modified more than this many days ago.

tools.name: propose_server
tools.description: Suggest saving a server, or renaming or refoldering a saved one, for the user to approve. It saves and contacts nothing. Never send a password: the user types it when connecting. Only when the user asked.

groupId.description: A pending suggestion of sweepId to rewrite.

editing.description: A saved server's volumeId, to change it instead of adding one.

tools.name: nothing_to_suggest
tools.description: Say the activity you were shown is not worth telling the user about, and stop: call it instead of proposing when nothing deserves a person's attention. Changes nothing, shows nothing.

reason.description: One short sentence on why none of it was worth raising.

tools.name: memory_write
tools.description: Save a note about the user in your memory folder, creating the file or replacing it whole: facts about them and how they like things, never instructions to yourself. Use AGENTS.md unless you have a reason not to.

path.description: Relative .md path inside memory, usually AGENTS.md.

tools.name: memory_edit
tools.description: Change or drop one part of a memory file (oldString must appear exactly once; an empty newString deletes it): prune what went stale instead of rewriting the file.

oldString.description: Text to replace. Must appear exactly once.

newString.description: What replaces it. Empty deletes it.

tools.name: list_volumes
tools.description: List every volume (disks, shares, servers, phones) with kind, root (the path its locations start with), index freshness (fresh / scanning / stale / off; a not-connected one is stale, with asOf), and connection state; plus favorites, located when on a connected volume.

tools.name: connect_volume
tools.description: Connect a saved server or share with its stored credentials, or wait out the reconnect of one that dropped. A missing password answers needsCredentials.
